With 0->3 already convolved, a conv on 1->3 adds a partly redundant parallel conv route into the output, shrinking its marginal gain.
An identity bypass on 0->3 eases optimisation of the deepened 0->1->2->3 conv chain, matching the residual-plus-deep-conv pattern of top NAS-Bench-201 cells.
A parallel conv route on 1->3 already supplies output capacity, so degrading 2->3 to pooling costs less.
If 0->2 already convolves, a conv on 1->2 is a partly redundant second learnable input to node 2, reducing its marginal benefit.
With 1->2 absent, 0->2 is node 2's only input, so making it a conv determines everything flowing through 2->3 and matters more.
A skip on 1->3 forwards node 1's features to the output, which is only valuable when node 1 holds learned conv features.
An identity bypass on 0->3 around a conv route ending at 2->3 forms a residual block, raising the skip's value relative to when 2->3 is weak.
Identity on 0->3 plus a conv branch through 1->3 forms a classic residual block, so the skip helps more when 1->3 convolves.
Removing node 2's direct input is more harmful when 2->3 holds a conv, because the conv's capacity is wasted on a weakened or empty node 2.
